issues.description: Resolver.resolve() postcondition silently weakened; returned requirements may no longer be fully prepared.
issues.detail: The resolver previously guaranteed every returned requirement had prepared=True and needs_more_preparation=False. That loop is deleted without restating the contract, shifting the obligation onto every caller. Any consumer (third-party, plugin, future command) relying on the old guarantee is silently broken. Document the new postcondition on resolve() or restore the invariant.

issues.description: prepare_linked_requirements_more is copy-pasted across three commands instead of centralized in a helper or resolver flag.
issues.detail: download.py, install.py, and wheel.py each independently invoke the same call after resolve(). This is three places to forget when a fourth command (e.g., lock) needs the same step. Either push it back into resolve() behind a dry_run flag, or extract a single shared helper. Sprinkled incantations are not decoupling.

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist caches metadata-only distribution with no invalidation after full download lands.
issues.detail: _fetch_metadata_only stores a metadata-only BaseDistribution in self._distribution; get_dist() prefers it over metadata_directory and local_file_path. After prepare_linked_requirements_more fully downloads the wheel, the stale metadata-only dist still wins. If the two diverge (RECORD, file list, install paths), silent wrong behavior follows. Invalidate _distribution on full prep or document the precedence rule.

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist introduced without docstrings, preconditions, postconditions, or invariants.
issues.detail: set_dist accepts any BaseDistribution with no constraints on when it is valid to call and no statement of what callers may assume. For a mutable cache on a long-lived object touched by resolver, preparer, and installer, the spec is the contract. Document that it stores a metadata-only view, may be superseded, and the precedence rule used by get_dist.

issues.description: download_info populated via direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir) when source_dir may be unset in metadata-only/dry-run mode.
issues.detail: At the point _fetch_metadata_only succeeds, nothing has been unpacked and req.source_dir is typically unset. direct_url_from_link's behavior with a missing source_dir is undemonstrated. With a VCS URL this could produce a malformed DirectUrl, silently corrupting pip lock / --report output. State the precondition or add a test covering dry-run + VCS + --report.

issues.description: No tests in the diff exercise the headline behavior (dry-run avoids full wheel download) or new precedence rules.
issues.detail: The PR's stated property — --dry-run no longer downloads full wheels when PEP 658 metadata exists — is a one-line functional assertion. The diff contains zero tests for that, for pip lock emitting download_info from metadata-only paths, or for the new set_dist/get_dist precedence. Add a test that fails without the patch and passes with it.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the intent is sound — eager full-download inside resolve() was a real defect, and deferring it for dry-run / pip lock is the right direction. But the execution silently weakens resolve()'s postcondition, scatters the replacement call across three command modules instead of one helper, and introduces a set_dist/get_dist cache with no invalidation when the full download eventually lands. Contracts for the new methods, the resolver/preparer boundary, and download_info's producers are undocumented. No tests exercise the headline behavior. NEEDS-WORK: document the new contracts, consolidate the call site, fix the cache invariant, and add a dry-run-no-download test.
